MIND. [1] [Arg. n.]
Loss of memory. θ Headache from dancing.
Impulsive, must walk very fast ; frequent turns of anxiety.
Apprehension when ready to go to church or to opera ; diarrhœa sets in.
   

SENSORIUM. [2] [Arg. n.]
Buzzing in ears ; general debility of limbs and trembling.
   

OUTER HEAD. [4] [Arg. n.]
Head feels much enlarged, or eye on affected side.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Arg. n.]
Intolerance of light. θ Want of accommodation.
Eyes red, shuns light, after straining them while sewing ; < in warm room, > in open air.
Dilated pupils. θ Want of accommodation.
Purulent ophthalmia.
Chemosis with strangulated vessels, most profuse purulent discharge, even cornea beginning to get hazy and looking as though it would slough.
Cornea opaque ; ulceration of cornea in newborn infants ; profuse purulent discharge from lids.
Acute granular conjunctivitis, conjunctiva intensely pink or scarlet, discharge profuse, inclined to be mucopurulent.
Ciliary blepharitis from being over a fire ; > from cold air and cold applications. θ Ectropion.
Blepharitis if lids are very red, thick and swollen, especially if complicated with granulations, conjunctivitis or some deeper inflammation of eye.
Discharge causing firm agglutination of lids in morning. θ Blepharitis.
Lids crusty, swollen, very sore and thick. θ Pannus.
   

UPPER FACE. [8] [Arg. n.]
Looks prematurely old ; also in cholera infantum.
Face : sunken, pale bluish ; leaden colored, with nausea ; yellow, dirty looking.
   

TASTE, SPEECH, TONGUE. [11] [Arg. n.]
Red, painful tip of tongue, papillæ erect, prominent.
   

PALATE AND THROAT. [13] [Arg. n.]
Uvula and fauces dark red.
Thick tenacious mucus in throat, obliging him to hawk ; causing slight hoarseness.
Sensation as if a splinter was lodged in throat, when swallowing, eructating,    

APPETITE, THIRST. DESIRES, AVERSIONS. [14] [Arg. n.]
Loss of appetite ; much thirst, or no thirst.
Irresistible desire for sugar.
   

EATING AND DRINKING. [15] [Arg. n.]
Fluids go "right through him." θ Cholera infantum, etc.
   

HICCOUGH, BELCHING, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. [16] [Arg. n.]
Most gastric ailments are accompanied by belching.
Belching after every meal ; stomach as if it would burst with wind ; belching difficult, finally air rushes out with great violence.
Eructation relieves.
Flatulence passes upward in quantities, inducing faintness. θ Dyspepsia.
   

SCROBICULUM AND STOMACH. [17] [Arg. n.]
Flatulent dyspepsia.
Gastrodynia.
Pain in left side of stomach, below short ribs, more intense during inspiration and on touching parts. θ Dyspepsia.
Gastric derangements are accompanied by belching.
   

ABDOMEN AND LOINS. [19] [Arg. n.]
Flatulence. θ Dyspepsia.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Arg. n.]
Diarrhœa as soon as he drinks.
Child is very fond of sugar, but diarrhœa results from eating it. θ Cholera infantum.
Masses of epithelium connected by muco-lymph, looking red or green and shreddy, with severe bearing down in hypogastrium ; advanced dysentery, with suspected ulceration.
Stools of green, fetid mucus, with noisy flatus at night ; green, brown, bloody, < after midnight ; slimy, watery, greenish, bloody, with tenesmus ; green, watery, sour taste in mouth.
Green stools ; sopor, large pupils.
   

URINARY ORGANS. [21] [Arg. n.]
Urine passed unconsciously and uninterruptedly.
Incontinence of urine at night, also by day.
Urging to urinate ; urine passes less easily and freely.
   

FEMALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [23] [Arg. n.]
Coition painful, followed by bleeding from vagina.
Prolapsus with ulceration of os or cervix.
Menses now too soon and at other times too late ; irregular. θ Prolapsus uteri.
Menses scanty. θ Asthma. θ Prolapsus uteri.
   

PREGNANCY. PARTURITION. LACTATION. [24] [Arg. n.]
During pregnancy stomach feels as if it would burst with wind ; head feels expanded.
   

VOICE AND LARYNX. TRACHEA AND BRONCHIA. [25] [Arg. n.]
Chronic laryngitis of singers ; raising voice causes cough.
   

LIMBS IN GENERAL. [34] [Arg. n.]
Lassitude, weariness of forearms and legs.
Trembling.
   

NERVES. [36] [Arg. n.]
Periodical trembling of body.
Convulsions preceded by great restlessness.
Any voluntary motion of body was for a long time impossible for him. θ Typhus.
Paraplegia from debilitating causes.
   

TIME. [38] [Arg. n.]
Worse at night : heat in head, headache ; nose stopped up ; throat dry ; gastralgia ; colic ; diarrhœa ; much urine ; cough ; hoarseness ; beating of heart ; epileptic attacks ; pains in chest, oppression ; spasms ; nervous ; itching of skin.
Day half, more cough ; night, diarrhœa.
   

TEMPERATURE AND WEATHER. [39] [Arg. n.]
Utter insensibility of body, except a sensitiveness of lowered temperature, even from removing clothes when dressing bed-sores. θ Typhus.
Asthma drives him to open window ; if windows are closed, he becomes restless ; at night he wakes up as if suffocating, runs to window to breathe.
They had to leave a window open, day and night, in March, for when it was shut patient became restless. θ Typhus.
Ophthalmia less ; stomach relieved in open air.
   

TISSUES. [44] [Arg. n.]
Bone affections.
   

TOUCH. PASSIVE MOTION. INJURIES. [45] [Arg. n.]
Erysipelatous bed-sore upon left shoulder, sacrum and both hip joints ; those on sacrum became black and hard. θ Typhus.
   

SKIN. [46] [Arg. n.]
Bluish-black eruption. θ In scarlet fever.
